Subject: SolarisCap post-incident package: RCA, timeline, and verification plan

Priya —

Thank you again for the flag and for routing the urgent jobs to fallback — that prevented a larger outage. Please find our concise post-incident package below; full artifacts are attached (PDF RCA, incident timeline CSV, and the runbook diff). I’ve kept this summary focused for your audit and operations review; happy to walk through any part on a call.

Executive summary (TL;DR)
- What happened: A regression in the autoscaler control loop caused transient over-sharding of model workers leading to a KV cache miss storm under our 512-token workload profile. The miss storm amplified latency and error rates for batched synchronous requests.
- Impact window: 2028-03-05T01:22:00Z to 2028-03-05T01:36:00Z (14 minutes).
- Customer-visible symptoms: ~18% of requests returned 5xx; median tail latency increased from 120ms to 1.5s for affected routes. No data leakage.
- Root cause: A logic change deployed in the autoscaler (commit a3f9c2) altered the worker sampling heuristic. Under a specific request-size distribution (heavy short-batch traffic + occasional 512-token requests) the estimator undershot available KV-cache warm workers, triggering cold-starts and repeated cache population attempts.

Timeline (high level)
- 01:20Z — Canary deploy of autoscaler change (a3f9c2).
- 01:22Z — Monitoring alert: spike in 5xx and tail latency on /v1/generate-batch.
- 01:24Z — Ops routed critical jobs to fallback cluster (SolarisCap routing rule executed).
- 01:27Z — Initial mitigations: rollback of autoscaler change and temporary preference for pre-warmed pools.
- 01:36Z — Error rates returned to baseline; ongoing verification through synthetic traffic.
- 03:00Z — Post-incident sanity checks and postmortem kickoff.

Immediate mitigations we applied
- Rolled back the autoscaler change to the prior stable commit.
- Forced a KV-cache priming job for affected pools and increased cache TTL from 5m to 15m for the next 24 hours.
- Temporarily increased the minimum warm pool size for routes serving SolarisCap to reduce cold-start exposure.

Action pack (owners & dates) — what we will do next
1) Autoscaler fix (root cause patch) — owner: David Kim (engineering) — ETA: 2028-03-12
   - Rework sampling heuristic to account for mixed-size workloads and add a safety clamp on worker downscaling.
2) Runbook and gating — owner: Tessa Morgan (SRE) — ETA: 2028-03-09
   - Add a pre-deploy regression test for KV cache amplification scenarios and a deploy gating rule for autoscaler changes.
3) Verification plan (customer-facing) — owner: Vanessa Ortiz (account) & David Kim — ETA: 2028-03-10
   - Shared synthetic test run with SolarisCap (3-day rolling window) and weekly verification for 30 days.
4) Compensation & SLA review — owner: Vanessa Ortiz (account) — ETA: 2028-03-07
   - Proposed one-time service credit covering affected window; will follow up with finance if accepted.
5) Long-term control (platform) — owner: Product/Infra — ETA: Q2 2028
   - Telemetry improvements for request-size-aware autoscaling and an automated KV-cache priming optimization.

Verification steps we propose for SolarisCap to accept closure
- Redwood will run the agreed synthetic test suite against your traffic profile and share results (link below).
- We will provide a runbook diff and a readout of the autoscaler patch in an ops review call.
- After 7 days of stable results (no recurrence at previously observed thresholds), we will request formal closure.

Attachments included
- solariscap_rca_summary_v1.pdf — detailed forensic analysis and logs
- incident_timeline_20280305.csv — per-minute event timeline and metrics
- runbook_changes_patch.diff — proposed runbook deltas for your SRE ingestion

Related artifacts and links
- Incident ticket: JIRA-RED-4521
- Shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cSOLARIS-RCA
- Support case: https://redwood.app/support/cases/CASE-8921

Next steps
- Vanessa: I’ll schedule a 30-minute verification call for Thu 2028-03-08 10:00 PT unless you prefer another slot.
- David/Tessa: please confirm owners and ETAs above; I’ll add them to the customer-facing action tracker once confirmed.

Thanks again — we take this seriously and will keep you closely updated.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
